title: Introduce timebound RBAC elevation, KMS region safety-net, and interactive audit playback
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: Provide a safer, auditable path for short-lived operator elevations and an auditable, replayable view of operator activity while enforcing KMS region constraints. This PR implements three coordinated features: (1) RBAC temporal elevations: a timebound, JIT elevation flow for operators that issues a signed short-lived elevation token (TTL default 15m) with optional canary approval gates and optional MFA requirement. Elevations are recorded in the decision-store and attached to subsequent request contexts so RBAC v2 decisions include elevation metadata. (2) KMS region safety-net: a middleware layer that detects requests whose requested CMK region does not match tenant residency policy and routes them to a region-compliant fallback KMS provider or rejects with an audit artifact. Fallback behavior is pluggable via config and integrates with the existing kms-allocator. It also emits a signed consent fragment (kms_consent_sig) included in audit envelopes when fallback is used. (3) Interactive audit playback: a compliance tool (backend + console) that can reconstruct an operator session as a read-only replay for auditors. Playback sanitizes secrets (masked by default), attaches elevation tokens and kms_consent_sig artifacts, and allows time-synced step-through with trace/span links. Design notes: Elevation tokens are JWT-like, signed by the operator-issuer key, include constrained scope and machine-readable reason, and are validated by the policy-evaluator with a short clock skew tolerance. The kms safety-net uses a policy-layer decision to determine allowed regions; when fallback occurs the request is annotated and remains subject to the same policy decision tree. Audit playback does not re-execute requests against live models or KMS; it replays stored request/response payloads and links to spans for deeper investigation. Migration/rollout: Feature gated behind flags: rbac.temporal_elevation.enabled, kms.region_safety_net.mode={off,alert,auto_fallback}, audit.playback.enabled. Default rollout: canary on 5% of operator traffic for two weeks, then staged 25/50/100. Backwards compatibility: if feature flags are off the platform behaves as before. Rollback: clear flag and invalidate outstanding elevation tokens via token blacklist endpoint; kms safety-net deactivates fallback routing. Security review: threat modeling completed in SEC-102; elevation issuance requires operator credential + optional MFA; audit playback access is RBAC-protected and logs audit accesses. Testing: unit tests for token lifecycle and policy-evaluator changes, integration tests covering fallback KMS routing with mock providers, end-to-end canary in perf-canary lab to measure latency. Observability: new metrics: rbac_elevations_issued, rbac_elevation_failures, kms_safetynet_fallbacks, audit_playback_accesses; logs include elevation_id and kms_consent_sig reference. Performance: measured median request P50 increase <2% under canary batching; KV cache unaffected. Compliance: audit artifacts include persistent signed blobs for legal retention; playback UI supports export of redacted transcripts. Documentation: added API docs for elevation endpoints, operator-runbook, and console playback guide. Known limitations: elevation tokens currently not chainable; cross-service elevation propagation requires callsite instrumentation (follow-up ENG-3560). The PR contains migration scripts to populate existing operator metadata store with an elevation_version column. Merge notes: squash merge; database migration applied in release window.

feat(kms): safety-net middleware and region fallback adapter
feat(audit): store elevation metadata and consent artifacts in audit-envelope

test: unit + integration coverage for elevation and kms fallback
docs: operator runbook and API reference for temporal elevation

review_comments: Sarah Kim: Please clarify the TTL expiry semantics when clock skew occurs. Suggest token validation allow 30s skew and include issued_at claim.
Maya Patel (author): Added issued_at claim handling and explicit skew tolerance in token_issuer.go (commit: feat(rbac): add skew tolerance).
Diego Alvarez: KMS fallback adapter looks good, but we need a clear audit artifact to show consent. Can we include the upstream provider id and signed fragment?
Maya Patel (author): kms_consent_sig includes provider_id, region, and HMAC over request_id; stored in envelope as consent_ref (see audit/store/entry_envelope.go).
Priya Ramesh: Playback UI should not allow exported raw payloads without redaction. Add a checkbox gating export with a required justification log entry.
Maya Patel (author): Implemented export gating and justification log; playback export now writes an audit_access_record entry.
release_notes: Adds short-lived RBAC elevations (JIT) with canary rollout, a region-aware KMS safety-net with configurable fallback and signed consent artifacts, and an interactive read-only audit playback tool for compliance review. Feature gated behind rbac.temporal_elevation.enabled and kms.region_safety_net.mode. No API breaking changes by default.
rollback_plan: Flip feature flags off, blacklist outstanding elevation tokens via /admin/elevation_blacklist, revert kms safety-net config to 'alert' mode to stop auto-fallback, and invalidate canary routing. DB migration reversible via rollback SQL included in migrations/20251103_rollback.sql.
follow_up_tasks: ENG-3591: make elevation tokens chainable for bounded delegation
DOC-210: audit-playback training material for compliance team
